# PEN-5017 — surface `enableGitHubPublishBroker` in the adapter config schema

PR: filed from [PEN-5017](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-5017)

## Files

- `src/server/config-schema.ts`
- `src/server/config-schema.test.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.github-publish-broker.test.ts`

## What changed

`getConfigSchema()` now returns a `toggle` field for
`enableGitHubPublishBroker`, default `false`. No behaviour change: the key was
already read by `buildJobManifest` (PEN-4933) and settable on an agent; it was
simply absent from the schema the UI renders, so the state of the gate was
legible only to whoever read `agents.adapterConfig` in the database.

## Why

The gate decides whether the GitHub push credential is mounted into the agent
container or into the `github-publish-broker` sidecar at uid 1001 — i.e. it is
the on/off switch of a credential boundary, not a preference. A reviewer asking
"is this agent brokered?" had no answer short of a database read, and PEN-3183
D1 stage 1 is about to set it `true` for real agents. Half of PEN-5017's
done-when is making that state auditable; this is that half.

## What this field is NOT

It is a **view**, not an enforcement point, and the hint and the comment above
it both say so. The key is pinned to agent provenance on the Paperclip server
side — `AGENT_SCOPE_ONLY_CONFIG_KEYS` in `server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`,
added in the same PR — because `mergeModelProfileAdapterConfig` overlays
`issue.assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig` last with no key allowlist, and
an agent can file an issue against itself. Without that pin an agent could have
rendered itself a pod with the credential back in its own container. Nothing in
this adapter enforces that, and reading the presence of this toggle as the
thing that makes it true would be exactly the overclaim PEN-3183 §8 prohibits.

The adapter-side half of the boundary — the broker is rendered if and only if
the config handed to `buildJobManifest` carries the flag — is unchanged and
stays asserted in `job-manifest.github-publish-broker.test.ts`.

## Second change in the same PR: the broker's image is now agent-scope

Found by Ally reviewing the first revision, and it is the more important half.

`buildJobManifest` resolved `image` off `ctx.config` — the **merged** run config
— and handed that image to `buildGitHubPublishBrokerSidecar`. The broker execs
`paperclip-github-token-env` and the broker runtime JS **out of that image**
with the push credential in its environment. Because an issue-scope
`assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig` is overlaid into the merged config,
an agent could file an issue against itself setting `image`, leave
`enableGitHubPublishBroker` pinned exactly as the server-side guard intends,
and still choose the code running at uid 1001 holding the token. The gate held;
the boundary did not.

The broker now resolves its image from `ctx.agent.adapterConfig` — the agent row
before any merge, and the one image value in that function with agent
provenance — using the same `asString(...) || selfPod.image` rule as before.

**The agent container deliberately keeps the merged value.** Once the broker is
rendered the agent container holds no GitHub credential at all, so what it runs
is its own business; only the credential-holding container must run
operator-chosen code. A test asserts that asymmetry so a later "fix" cannot
quietly pin both and look correct.

**Divergence is allowed, not refused.** If a lower scope points the agent
container at a different image, a socket-protocol mismatch fails loudly at
publish time with no credential in it. Throwing instead would hand every actor
able to assign an issue a way to fail this agent's dispatches — the trade
PEN-3183 §7.5 explicitly declines for the gate key.

Zero rendered-output change today: the broker is only rendered when the gate is
on, and it is off everywhere.
